children: The 3,200 MW ultra-supercritical plant at Chapar in Dhubri district is scheduled for phased commissioning from December 2030

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Sunday laid the foundation stone for Adani Power's 3,200 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power plant (USTPP) at Chapar in Dhubri district, lower Assam. The project has an investment of Rs 48,000 crore and is expected to generate 5,000 jobs.
The Chapar plant will comprise four units of 800 MW each and will use ultra-supercritical technology. Commissioning is scheduled to take place in phases from December 2030.

The project is part of the Adani group's planned investment of Rs 63,000 crore in Assam. Of this amount, Rs 48,000 crore is allocated to the Chapar power plant, while Rs 15,000 crore is earmarked for two pumped storage plants with a combined capacity of 2,700 MW.
The company said investments across sectors in Assam would exceed Rs 80,000 crore, with projects moving towards execution over the next three to four years.

Speaking at the foundation stone ceremony, Sarma said the Chapar project would contribute to Assam's energy infrastructure and economic activity. He also said the state would benefit from increased SGST revenues.

Jeet Adani, Director, Adani Group, said the Chapar plant would become the largest power generation asset in the Northeast and would support electricity supply for industries, businesses and households.
The company said the Chapar project is expected to be the largest power generation asset in the Northeast once completed.
